transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is… I’ve just stopped caring about things I used to actually look forward to. My fishing gear’s been sitting untouched in the garage, I don’t want to spend time in the woodshop anymore—it feels like a chore—and even when my kids ask me to play chess, I’m just kind of going through the motions.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about a year and seven months now. It really started after my wife’s health problems changed everything at home.
Have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, since these changes began?
I don’t really know if I’d say that. I mean, I haven’t been myself, but I’m not sure I’d call it feeling depressed most of the day every day. It’s more like… I just don’t have much in me lately.
Have you felt like you don’t have much energy or that even small tasks take a lot out of you most days?

Yeah. Most days I’m worn out way earlier than I should be. By midmorning it can feel like I’ve already put in a full shift, and at work even just walking the project or taking stairs with the crew feels like I’m carrying wet concrete around.
Have you experienced days where you felt down or sad most of the time, not just briefly, and that feeling lasted for weeks at a time over the past year and a half?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had bad days, yeah, but I haven’t kept track of whether it was most of the day or for weeks at a time. It’s more that I just haven’t felt like myself for a long while.
Over the past year and a half, have you had days where your mood has been low or sad most of the time, not just once in a while?
I’m not sure I can say it that clearly. I’ve had days where I felt pretty low, yeah, but I don’t know if it was most of the time that day or just on and off. It’s all kind of blurred together.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like fishing or working in the woodshop, don’t give you the same satisfaction or pleasure anymore?

Yeah… I have. I just don’t really care about the things I used to look forward to. My fishing gear’s been sitting in the garage untouched, and when I go into the woodshop it feels more like another job than something I enjoy. Even when my kids want me to play chess, I’ll do it, but I’m mostly just going through the motions.
Has there been a time in the past year and a half when you completely stopped getting any pleasure or interest from almost all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

Yeah. I mean, that’s probably the main thing I’ve noticed. I just kind of stopped caring about the stuff I used to look forward to. My fishing gear’s still sitting in the garage, I don’t use it. The woodshop feels like a chore now. Even when my kids ask me to play chess, I’ll sit down and do it, but I’m not really into it… I’m just going through the motions.

Was there ever a specific time in the past year and a half when you completely stopped getting any pleasure or interest from almost all activities—even the ones you used to really enjoy—for at least two weeks straight?

Yeah… there was. I can’t give you an exact date, but it went on longer than two weeks. I just stopped caring about the things I used to look forward to. My fishing stuff stayed untouched in the garage, the woodshop felt like a chore, and even with my kids asking me to play chess, I’d do it but I wasn’t really there… just going through the motions.

Was there a time when you completely stopped getting any pleasure or interest from almost all activities—even the ones you used to really enjoy—for at least two weeks without it getting better at all?

Yeah… it didn’t really lift for a while. I just stopped caring about the things I used to look forward to. My fishing gear stayed untouched in the garage, the woodshop felt like work, not something I wanted to do, and even when my kids wanted to play chess, I’d sit there but I was mostly just going through the motions.

Was there a continuous period of at least two weeks when you completely stopped getting any pleasure or interest from almost all activities—even the ones you used to really enjoy—without any improvement at all during that time?

Yes. It was steady for at least a couple weeks, probably longer. I just… didn’t care about anything I used to look forward to. My fishing gear just sat in the garage, I didn’t touch the woodshop because it felt like a chore, and even when my kids wanted to play chess, I’d sit there but I wasn’t really into it. Just going through the motions.
